Start with the expanded examples. Open further examples for options and alternative R approaches.

mi

Extract first completed dataset

Stata 

mi extract 1

R mice 

mice::complete(imp, 1)

Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. R mids metadata and storage structures differ from Stata MI data styles.

Stata reference · R reference

Chained-equation imputation using pmm

Stata 

mi impute chained (pmm, knn(5)) x z = y, add(3) rseed(108) burnin(10)

R mice 

mice::mice(data, m = 3, maxit = 10, method = "pmm", seed = 108, donors = 5L, printFlag = FALSE)

Differs from Stata Fresh FCS imputation of x and z using each other and complete y. These packages implement the same model families but use different random-number streams. R performs 10 iterations per chain; Stata uses burnin(10). Assess convergence rather than treating this illustrative schedule as sufficient.

Stata reference · R reference

mi impute chained (regress) x z = y, add(3) rseed(108) burnin(10)

R mice

Differs from Stata Fresh FCS imputation of x and z using each other and complete y. These packages implement the same model families but use different random-number streams. R performs 10 iterations per chain; Stata uses burnin(10). Assess convergence rather than treating this illustrative schedule as sufficient.

Pooled estimates with ninety-percent intervals

Stata 

mi estimate, level(90): regress y x z

R mice 

summary(mice::pool(with(imp, stats::lm(y ~ x + z))), conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = .90)

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Uses mice's pooled small-sample degrees-of-freedom rules.

Stata reference · R reference

Pool logistic-regression coefficients

Stata 

mi estimate: logit binary x z

R mice 

mice::pool(with(imp, stats::glm(binary ~ x + z, family = stats::binomial())))

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Pool on the log-odds scale before exponentiating.

Stata reference · R reference

Rubin pooling of an imputed continuous mean

Stata 

mi estimate: mean x

R mice 

{ completed <- mice::complete(imp, "all"); Q <- vapply(completed, function(d) mean(d$x), numeric(1)); U <- vapply(completed, function(d) stats::var(d$x) / nrow(d), numeric(1)); mice::pool.scalar(Q, U, n = nrow(data), k = 1) }

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Within-imputation mean variances and complete-data sample sizes are explicit.

Stata reference · R reference

Pool Poisson-regression coefficients

Stata 

mi estimate: poisson count x z

R mice 

mice::pool(with(imp, stats::glm(count ~ x + z, family = stats::poisson())))

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Pool log-rate coefficients; assess overdispersion separately.

Stata reference · R reference

Pool coefficient vectors and covariance matrices directly

Stata 

mi estimate: regress y x z

R mitools 

{ fits <- lapply(mice::complete(imp, "all"), function(d) stats::lm(y ~ x + z, data = d)); mitools::MIcombine(lapply(fits, stats::coef), lapply(fits, stats::vcov), df.complete = stats::df.residual(fits[[1L]])) }

Differs from Stata Pool regression coefficients and covariance by Rubin rules with df.complete=n-3 for intercept,x,z. This preserves finite complete-data degrees of freedom instead of MIcombine default infinity.

Stata reference · R reference

Binary logistic chained-equation imputation

Stata 

mi impute chained (logit) category (pmm, knn(5)) x z = y, add(3) burnin(10)

R mice 

{ methods <- mice::make.method(data); methods["category"] <- "logreg"; methods[c("x", "z")] <- "pmm"; mice::mice(data, m = 3, maxit = 10, method = methods, seed = 131, donors = 5L, printFlag = FALSE) }

Differs from Stata Data contains only y, x, z and category; y is complete, category is a binary/unordered/ordered factor as stated. The visible method vector selects its categorical model and PMM for x,z. Three fresh FCS imputations use 10 iterations; inspect convergence. Random draws and separation safeguards differ across software.

Stata reference · R reference

Derive a nonlinear variable consistently in each completed dataset

Stata 

mi passive: generate square = x^2

R mice 

lapply(mice::complete(imp, action = "all"), function(d) transform(d, square = x^2))

Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Post-imputation derivation is appropriate when the transform is not needed as an imputation predictor; otherwise use passive imputation within the chain.

Stata reference · R reference

Combine repeated complete-data Wald tests

Stata 

mi test x

R mice 

{ full <- with(imp, stats::lm(y ~ x + z)); reduced <- with(imp, stats::lm(y ~ z)); mice::D1(full, reduced) }

D1 pools coefficient estimates and covariance matrices for a multivariate MI Wald test, as Stata mi test does. Use the same coefficient ordering and complete-data degrees of freedom; D2 pools test statistics and is a different rule.

Stata reference · R reference

Pooled multivariate Wald comparison

Stata 

mi test x z

R mice 

{ full <- with(imp, stats::lm(y ~ x + z)); reduced <- with(imp, stats::lm(y ~ 1)); mice::D1(full, reduced) }

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. D1 combines nested-model Wald information; coefficients must have consistent ordering.
